editorial.headline: Upstream Essential Oils, Open Nationally and Not Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20294 covers the making of essential oils from spices, flowers, leaves, roots, bark, resin, fruit, seeds, and other plant materials.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20294 is the upstream essential-oil manufacturing activity. In practical terms, it is where raw aromatic plant material becomes oil: ginger, cinnamon, coriander, clove, cardamom, nutmeg, jasmine, ylang-ylang, vetiver root, citronella, lemongrass, patchouli, sandalwood, agarwood, eucalyptus, peppermint, spice oils, and oils drawn from resin, bark, roots, leaves, fruit, seeds, and flowers that are not otherwise placed elsewhere. The centre of gravity is production, not retail presentation: the record points to the making of the oil itself, from plant inputs into an essential-oil output.

The activity is broadly usable across business sizes. The record opens it to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, which means the same activity classification can describe a small producer as well as a larger industrial operator, provided the registered activity is still the making of upstream essential oils. That range matters because the activity is not framed only for artisanal production or only for large factories; the scale depends on the registrant, while the defining scope remains the same manufacturing activity.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clean: the record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives a pma_max_asing of 100%. In plain English, the national record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to 100%, with the cited source listed as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower foreign-stake ceiling in the slim record, and no extra national condition is stated here, so the editorial picture should stay disciplined: the national PMA reading is open at the recorded ceiling.

Bali is also not shown as blocked in this record. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and l4_bali_blocked is false. The reason is specific: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, but this activity is not caught by that block on the record supplied. So the honest national-vs-Bali conclusion is simple: nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, and not blocked for Bali PMA registration on the supplied Bali moratorium check.
